title: Ordinary and completed inverse-image coefficient comparison towers
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and let $g:s\to s$ be any scheme automorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Work on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For each finite coefficient field $F\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, let $\mathcal O_F$ be its valuation ring with a chosen uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], put $R_F=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,s}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and write $G_F=g^{-1}$ with the $R_F$-action transported through $c_F^{-1}$ [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Sections $\Gamma(s,-)$ are termwise sections passed to derived categories [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact].

For finite $E\subset L\subset M$, put $C_{L/E}H=H\otimes^L_{R_E}R_L$ on the unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and use the canonical natural inverse-image tensor comparison $b_{L/E,H}:C_{L/E}G_EH\xrightarrow{\sim}G_LC_{L/E}H$ of [lem-weil-isomorphism-scalar-tensor-kflat-model]. Let $a^C_H:C_{M/L}C_{L/E}H\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{M/E}H$ be the ordinary tensor associator of [lem-weil-point-derived-tensor-tower-coherence]. For every $H\in D(R_E)$,
$$b_{M/E,H}a^C_{G_EH}=G_M(a^C_H)b_{M/L,C_{L/E}H}C_{M/L}(b_{L/E,H}).$$
On a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], both sides have local value $g^{-1}(x\otimes a_0b_0)$ on $((y\otimes a)\otimes b)$, where $y=g^{-1}x$, $a=c_L(g^{-1}a_0)$ and $b=c_M(g^{-1}b_0)$. The unit comparison $b_{E/E,H}$ is the identity under the ordinary multiplication identifications.

For $H\in D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], write $T_{L/E}H=H\widehat\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Use exactly $\chi_{L/E,H}:C_{L/E}H\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{L/E}H$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] and
$$\beta_{L/E,H}=G_L(\chi_{L/E,H})b_{L/E,H}\chi_{L/E,G_EH}^{-1}$$
of [lem-weil-isomorphism-comparison-scalar-extension]. The objects $G_EH$ are constructible and derived complete [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback]. Let $A_H:T_{M/L}T_{L/E}H\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{M/E}H$ be exactly the $\chi$-conjugated ordinary associator specified in [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. Then
$$\beta_{M/E,H}A_{G_EH}=G_M(A_H)\beta_{M/L,T_{L/E}H}T_{M/L}(\beta_{L/E,H}).$$
For the sections comparisons $\varphi_{L/E,H}=(\Gamma(s,\chi_{L/E,H})\theta_{L/E,H})^{-1}$ of that same node, put $\psi_{L/E,H}=\varphi_{L/E,G_EH}\Gamma(s,\beta_{L/E,H})^{-1}$. In $D(\mathcal O_M)$,
$$\psi_{M/E,H}\Gamma(s,G_MA_H)=a^{\mathrm{mod}}(\psi_{L/E,H}\otimes1)\psi_{M/L,T_{L/E}H},$$
where $a^{\mathrm{mod}}$ is the module associator $((n\otimes a)\otimes b)\mapsto n\otimes ab$. For $L=E$, both $\beta$ and $\psi$ are the identity under the canonical multiplication and derived-completeness identifications. All maps in these equalities are the specified maps, not newly chosen comparison isomorphisms.

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to H$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-weil-isomorphism-scalar-tensor-kflat-model], $G_EP$, $P\otimes_{R_E}R_L$ and $G_EP\otimes_{R_E}R_L$ are flat-term K-flat; applying it again at $L\subset M$ computes all the successive $b$ maps on these same models. The associators on these models are exactly the multiplication maps of [lem-weil-point-derived-tensor-tower-coherence]. For a local generator $((y\otimes a)\otimes b)$ as in the statement, the left route first multiplies $a,b$ and then gives $g^{-1}(x\otimes a_0b_0)$. The right route gives $g^{-1}(x\otimes a_0)\otimes b$, then $g^{-1}((x\otimes a_0)\otimes b_0)$, then $g^{-1}(x\otimes a_0b_0)$. To justify the coefficient multiplication here, the structure maps commute with coefficient inclusions: reduce at every level, use clause (3) of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], and then use the defining projections of $c_F$ in [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Equality of the projections gives equality into their inverse limit. Thus $c_M^{-1}(ab)$ is the image of $g^{-1}(a_0b_0)$. Sheaf tensor is sheafified presheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], so agreement on these local generators implies equality of sheaf maps in every degree. These are chain maps by the cited K-flat model and associator statements. Passing this equality to the derived category proves the ordinary tower equation for every $H$; their stated resolution independence and naturality give the specified maps, without any completeness hypothesis.

proof.text: For $L=E$, the local formula in [lem-weil-isomorphism-scalar-tensor-kflat-model] sends $y\otimes r$ to $g^{-1}(x\otimes r_0)$. Source multiplication gives $ry$; target multiplication gives $g^{-1}(r_0x)=ry$ for the transported action. Hence $b_{E/E}$ is the identity under multiplication. This degreewise equality passes to the derived unit identifications of [lem-weil-point-derived-tensor-tower-coherence].

proof.text:
Now take $H\in D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$. The objects $G_FK$ stay constructible and complete by [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback], and scalar extensions stay constructible by [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible]. Thus every $\chi$, $\beta$ and iterated $\varphi$ below is defined and invertible by [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison, lem-weil-isomorphism-comparison-scalar-extension, lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. Abbreviate $C_1=C_{L/E}$, $C_2=C_{M/L}$, $C_3=C_{M/E}$ and similarly $T_i,b_i,\chi_i,\beta_i$. Put $U_K=\chi_{2,T_1K}C_2(\chi_{1,K})$. The specified integral associator is
$$A_K=\chi_{3,K}a^C_K U_K^{-1}.$$
Precompose each side of the claimed $\beta$ tower equation with $U_{G_EH}$. The left side becomes $G_M(\chi_{3,H})b_{3,H}a^C_{G_EH}$. For the right side, substitute $\beta_i=G(\chi_i)b_i\chi_i^{-1}$, and use the two naturality equations
$$T_2(\beta_{1,H})\chi_{2,T_1G_EH}=\chi_{2,G_LT_1H}C_2(\beta_{1,H}),$$
$$b_{2,T_1H}C_2(G_L\chi_{1,H})=G_M(C_2\chi_{1,H})b_{2,C_1H}.$$
Cancelling adjacent inverse comparisons gives
$$G_M(A_H U_H)b_{2,C_1H}C_2(b_{1,H})=G_M(\chi_{3,H})G_M(a^C_H)b_{2,C_1H}C_2(b_{1,H}).$$
The ordinary tower equation in Step 1 equates these expressions. Cancel the isomorphism $U_{G_EH}$ to obtain the completed tower equation for exactly the stated $\beta$ and $A$.

proof.text:
Write $\Gamma=\Gamma(s,-)$ and keep the indices $1,2,3$ of Step 3. Sections induce a functor on these derived categories by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. Rearranging Step 3 gives
$$\beta_{3,H}^{-1}G_M(A_H)=A_{G_EH}T_2(\beta_{1,H}^{-1})\beta_{2,T_1H}^{-1}.$$
Apply $\Gamma$ and multiply by $\varphi_{3,G_EH}$. The tower equation of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] rewrites the result as
$$\psi_{3,H}\Gamma(G_MA_H)=a^{\mathrm{mod}}(\varphi_{1,G_EH}\otimes1)\varphi_{2,T_1G_EH}\Gamma(T_2\beta_{1,H}^{-1})\Gamma(\beta_{2,T_1H}^{-1}).$$
The same node states naturality on derived morphisms. At $\beta_{1,H}^{-1}:G_LT_1H\to T_1G_EH$ it gives
$$\varphi_{2,T_1G_EH}\Gamma(T_2\beta_{1,H}^{-1})=(\Gamma(\beta_{1,H}^{-1})\otimes1)\varphi_{2,G_LT_1H}.$$
Substitution leaves $a^{\mathrm{mod}}(\psi_{1,H}\otimes1)\psi_{2,T_1H}$, which is the claimed sections equation. Every factor has the displayed source and target; no choice of a new sections comparison enters.

proof.text: For $L=E$, let $\mu_K:C_{E/E}K\to K$ be multiplication and $u_K:T_{E/E}K\to K$ the derived-completeness identification. By [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], $u_K\chi_{E/E,K}=\mu_K$. Substitution in the specified $\beta$ formula of [lem-weil-isomorphism-comparison-scalar-extension], followed by the multiplication identity of Step 2, gives $G_E(u_H)\beta_{E/E,H}=u_{G_EH}$. Thus $\beta$ is the identity under these identifications. The unit assertion of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] makes $\varphi_{E/E,G_EH}$ the identity under the same identifications; the definition $\psi=\varphi_G\Gamma(\beta)^{-1}$ then makes $\psi$ the identity as well.
